why_next: Decompression-normalization format-invariance is validated at localhost synthetic level across 3 content types × 3 sizes under brotli/gzip compression. The sole remaining blocker for decompression-normalization product readiness is real CDN infrastructure survival, which introduces fundamentally different non-determinism (edge quality selection, caching, chunked encoding, Accept-Encoding negotiation) not present in localhost testing. This question is orthogonal to the current localhost measurement — it tests a different environment, not a repetition of the same substrate.

established: Decompression-normalization (SHA256 on decompressed body + status) preserves body-only discrimination >= 0.3 for JSON, HTML, and XML at nominal 1KB/10KB/100KB under localhost brotli (quality 4-8) and gzip compression without CDN noise. Discrimination is 0.5 across all 9 content-type×size combinations (audit PASS, all 6 decision conditions pass).
Algorithm equivalence confirmed: |brotli_decompressed - gzip_decompressed| = 0.0 for all 18 type×size pairs. Decompressed bodies are algorithm-invariant.
Determinism confirmed: decompressed hash variation all_same=true for all 288 state×type×size×baseline cells. Within-state decompressed hashes are identical across 20 repetitions.

Decompression path is actually exercised: Content-Encoding br/gzip on all 5760 observations, decompression latency scales with payload size (0.015ms at 1KB to 0.21ms at 100KB for brotli). Parent MEASUREMENT_INVALID infrastructure failure resolved.

Compressed-only brotli discrimination is lower than decompressed (0.15-0.34 vs 0.5), confirming decompression is necessary for format-invariance. Gzip compressed discrimination equals decompressed (0.5) because gzip produces deterministic output (unique_count=1/20).

Structural discrimination ceiling is 0.5 due to 3-way error collapse in mock server design (no_auth/expired_token/invalid_token share identical error bodies). This is a property of the test environment, not the mechanism.
Parent EXP-RUNTIME-35137033384 claim ceiling (1KB JSON under synthetic CDN-noise proxy) stands and is expanded to multi-format multi-size under localhost compression.
rejected: Brotli quality diversity (unique compressed hashes per state) does not increase from 1KB to 100KB for repetitive padded content (avg 2.33 at both sizes). This is an artifact of repetitive padding content compressing identically across sizes, not evidence that brotli quality levels are irrelevant. The question of whether quality diversity increases with natural (non-padded) content remains open.
Decompression-normalization was NOT tested on real CDN infrastructure — all results are localhost mock server only. No inference to Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai edge behavior is justified.

do_not_assume: Do NOT assume decompression-normalization is production-ready — real CDN infrastructure is untested and is the critical remaining blocker.

Do NOT assume the structural discrimination ceiling of 0.5 applies to production environments — it is a property of the 3-way error collapse mock design. Real auth middleware may have different error response patterns.
Do NOT assume brotli quality diversity is irrelevant because it did not scale with repetitive padding — natural content may show different scaling behavior.
Do NOT assume the localhost decompression latency (0.015-0.21ms) represents production cost — real CDN latency includes network, edge computation, and negotiation overhead.
Do NOT assume format-invariance extends to binary content types, compressed data formats, or content types with variable encoding.
